name: A linear graph is struck out for an S-curve
looks: A position-over-time graph draws a straight diagonal line, a hand-drawn label and strike-through calling it out as the wrong way ("linear = robotic"); the line redraws as a soft S-curve, and a row of small boxes beneath marches along a timeline, bunching and spreading to match the curve's changing speed.
build: Straight line draws on first (`strokeDashoffset`); the annotation label and its strike-through line draw on together just after, in a hand-wobbled stroke distinct from the graph's clean lines. The line then redraws as a cubic-bezier S-curve over the same path; the marching boxes' x-spacing is sampled from the curve's local slope so they visibly bunch where it's slow and spread where it's fast.
sound: A dry tick as the straight line draws, a marker-pen scribble on the strike-through, a soft rising tone as the S-curve redraws, a patter of ticks under the marching boxes.
prompt: Draw a straight position-over-time line, label and strike it out by hand as the wrong, robotic way, then redraw the same line as a soft S-curve, and show a row of small boxes marching along a timeline beneath it, bunching and spreading to match the curve's changing speed so the effect of the easing is visible, not just the graph.
